chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Jabala from Abu al-Mi'za from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who performed tawaf around the Kaaba, then went out to al-Safa and performed tawaf around it, then mentioned that something remained of his tawaf. He ordered him to return to the Kaaba to complete what remained of his tawaf, then return to al-Safa to complete what remained. I said to him, 'What if he performed tawaf around al-Safa and left the Kaaba?' He said, 'He returns to the Kaaba and performs tawaf around it, then he faces the tawaf of al-Safa.' I said to him, 'What is the difference between these two?' He said, 'Because he has entered into something of the tawaf, and this one has not entered into anything of it.'

And it is not permissible for the Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu') to advance the Hajj tawaf before going to Mina and Arafat. And whenever he does that, he does not count that tawaf. And it is permissible for the old man, the weak person, and the woman who fears menstruation to advance it. That which indicates this is what has been narrated:

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa (one of the hills between which Sa'i is performed)
key_terms.طَوَافَ الْحَجِّ: Hajj tawaf (the specific circumambulation for Hajj)
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat (the plain where the standing at Arafat occurs)
key_terms.يَدُلُّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ: That which indicates this (introductory phrase for evidence)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on completing incomplete tawaf and when must the Hajj tawaf be performed for Mutamatti'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between interrupting an ongoing tawaf versus delaying its commencement, emphasizing that the former incurs a specific corrective action while the latter does not. The narration further establishes the general rule that the Hajj tawaf for a Mutamatti' must follow the standing at Arafat, with a practical concession for the elderly, weak, and women fearing menstruation to perform it beforehand. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on both ritual precision and ease (rukhas) in Hajj obligations.
